statement: In documented Māori creation traditions, Ranginui/Rangi (sky) and Papatūānuku/Papa (earth) are primal parents whose children separate them, bringing the world of light into being; multiple Māori versions exist.

sources.citation: Te Ahukaramū Charles Royal, “Māori creation traditions” and “Papatūānuku – the land,” Te Ara Encyclopedia of New Zealand.
sources.author: Te Ahukaramū Charles Royal
sources.venue: Te Ara Encyclopedia of New Zealand

sources.citation: Rāwiri Taonui, “Ranginui – the sky,” Te Ara Encyclopedia of New Zealand.
sources.author: Rāwiri Taonui
sources.venue: Te Ara Encyclopedia of New Zealand

does_not_demonstrate: Motif similarity with another tradition does not by itself demonstrate borrowing, common ancestry, or direct transmission.
notes: The entity deliberately describes multiple documented versions rather than presenting one account as a universal Māori canon.
